facts.fact: Minister Haliki Choua Mahamat said on 2026-10-09 that Chad has about 6,000 km of optical fibre, with a target of 14,000 km; the text does not say which regions it links.
Minister Haliki Choua Mahamat told the World Bank on 2026-09-15 that national fibre coverage is incomplete, with six provinces still not connected by fibre, and about 8,000 km still to deploy.

Citing the World Bank's June 2023 diagnostic, the national backbone has three axes (west, south, east), is almost wholly state-owned, operated by Sotel Tchad and Sudachad, and mainly links southern and eastern localities to N'Djamena.
Citing the World Bank's June 2023 diagnostic, two projects were under way: PMICE (1,200 km of fibre) and the Trans-Saharan backbone (550 km, Massaguet to N'Guigmi in Niger).

systems.tiers: operated by Sotel Tchad and Sudachad

facts.fact: At a ministerial review on 19 May 2026 the PMICE coordinator reported 1,275 km of fibre deployed so far on the national backbone works, with Huawei as contractor under Gulf Consultancy supervision; the document does not say it is in service.

DTS works (started 2023, EU-funded 29m euro) link Chad to Niger and are slowed; presented as a cross-border link, not the national backbone. No fact.

facts.fact: Ecofin reports the Chadian ministry said a 1,200 km national fibre-optic backbone, part of PMICE Phase I, was provisionally accepted at Sarh on 2025-12-20 and is now considered operational.

note: Work on the N'Djamena-Mbere route has not begun.
The Trans-Sahara backbone is a proposed cross-border project, not a national backbone.

facts.fact: Russell Southwood says Safitel's fibre runs from N'Djamena to Moundou, Doba and Abeche and connects 26 cities and towns, and all major cities are connected, while routes in the south-east remain unbuilt.
Minister Haliki Choua Mahamat told the ITU PP-26 that of a 14,000 km optical fibre target by 2030, 4,400 km are completed, 2,700 km are in progress and 6,900 km remain to be financed.

note: Only a joint letter of interest to the World Bank for a cross-border link; no agreement, works or service stated.
